speaker: narrator
text: What if prices dropped *every minute* you waited?

speaker: narrator
text: Jay just inherited his grandma's toy shop. *Penny's*.

speaker: narrator
text: It's tiny. It's dusty. And it's *empty*.

speaker: bit
text: Rent is due Monday. *Nine thousand* dollars.

speaker: hero
text: Bit, I have *two hundred* dollars.

speaker: bit
text: Then we need Black Friday. And a *crazy idea*.

speaker: bit
text: Boston, nineteen oh nine. A store with *falling prices*.

speaker: bit
text: Unsold after twelve days? Twenty five percent *off*.

speaker: bit
text: Still unsold? It went to *charity*.

speaker: hero
text: Days are too slow. What about... *minutes*?

speaker: narrator
text: So they invent *the Drop*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia, his best friend, prints *five hundred* flyers.

speaker: friend
text: Black Friday. Six a.m. Prices fall *till midnight*.

speaker: narrator
text: Friday morning, the line wraps around the *block*.

speaker: narrator
text: Six o'clock. The doors open. The clock *starts*.

speaker: narrator
text: Every price tag in the store starts *falling*.

speaker: hero
text: Okay, everyone. Go! *Buy things*!

speaker: narrator
text: But nobody moves. Not *one* person.

speaker: bit
text: Jay... they're not shopping. They're *waiting*.

speaker: narrator
text: Seven a.m. Everything is ten percent *off*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nine a.m. Thirty percent. Still *nothing*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit, why is nobody *buying*?

speaker: bit
text: It's a *Dutch auction*. You built one by accident.

speaker: bit
text: Price starts high. Falls until someone *says yes*.

speaker: bit
text: Dutch flower markets sell flowers with a *falling clock*.

speaker: bit
text: Wait too long, and someone else *takes it*.

speaker: narrator
text: In the corner, a kid stares at a *robot*.

speaker: kid
text: I'm Theo. My sister turns seven *on Sunday*.

speaker: narrator
text: The robot costs forty dollars. Theo has *twelve*.

speaker: bit
text: At this speed, it hits twelve at *two p.m.*

speaker: kid
text: Then I'll wait. I'm *very* good at waiting.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia picks up the ugliest sweater in the *shop*.

speaker: friend
text: Forty bucks? Hmm. *Not yet*.

speaker: narrator
text: By the door, a man in sunglasses *smiles*.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. That man has been inside *since midnight*.

speaker: hero
text: We opened at six. How is that *possible*?

speaker: bit
text: Not in the store. In our *website*.

speaker: narrator
text: His name is Flip. He flips toys *for money*.

speaker: gambler
text: I buy low. I sell high. It's called *business*.

speaker: bit
text: His bot has four hundred toys *in its cart*.

speaker: hero
text: Every toy in the shop? At *what price*?

speaker: bit
text: The lowest price the Drop allows. *One cent*.

speaker: hero
text: Four hundred toys for four dollars? Stop *the Drop*!

speaker: friend
text: Jay, five hundred flyers said *until midnight*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay looks at the crowd. They look *back*.

speaker: hero
text: If I stop now, they'll tear it *apart*.

speaker: gambler
text: Relax, kid. I'm a *patient* man.

speaker: narrator
text: Noon. Prices are sixty percent off. Still *no sales*.

speaker: narrator
text: The robot toy falls to *sixteen dollars*.

speaker: kid
text: Sixteen. Almost. I have twelve. *Almost*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia checks her sweater. Twenty dollars. *Not yet*.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. Flip's bot just picked *the robot*.

speaker: hero
text: Theo. The bot wants your robot. Buy it *now*.

speaker: kid
text: I only have twelve. I *can't*.

speaker: narrator
text: Somewhere, a computer counts down to *one cent*.

speaker: narrator
text: Two p.m. The robot hits *twelve dollars*.

speaker: kid
text: Twelve! I have twelve! I'm *buying* it!

speaker: narrator
text: Theo runs to the counter. His coins *spill*.

speaker: narrator
text: He counts. Ten. Eleven. One coin is *missing*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit, can't we just give him *one dollar*?

speaker: bit
text: The Drop is automatic. Three. Two. *One*.

speaker: narrator
text: Three p.m. Every price hits *one cent*.

speaker: narrator
text: In one second, Flip's bot buys *everything*.

speaker: narrator
text: The robot. The puzzles. Even Mia's *ugly sweater*.

speaker: friend
text: It was going to be *ten bucks*!

speaker: narrator
text: The crowd shuffles out. The shop is *silent*.

speaker: bit
text: Total sales today. Four dollars. And *zero cents*.

speaker: narrator
text: Theo stands at the counter. *Eleven dollars* in hand.

speaker: kid
text: It's okay. Robots are for *babies* anyway.

speaker: hero
text: Theo, wait. I'm *so* sorry.

speaker: narrator
text: The door chimes. Flip walks out *whistling*.

speaker: gambler
text: Thanks for the sale. Want them back? *Triple price*.

speaker: narrator
text: Five p.m. Flip's toys are *online*.

speaker: hero
text: A hundred twenty dollars. For *Theo's* robot.

speaker: friend
text: And my sweater. Ninety *nine* dollars!

speaker: narrator
text: Jay drops into Grandma's old chair. Something *crinkles*.

speaker: narrator
text: A shoebox. Old price tags. And a *note*.

speaker: hero
text: Two people. Today I made *one*. Flip.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. Can I read the flyer *again*?

speaker: friend
text: I made those flyers. They're *perfect*.

speaker: bit
text: Tiny print, bottom corner. Mia, did you *write* this?

speaker: friend
text: Grandma Penny's rule. I copied it from *her sign*.

speaker: narrator
text: Flip's four hundred toys are still on *our shelf*.

speaker: hero
text: He has to come and get them. *Before midnight*.

speaker: bit
text: And his bot used four hundred *accounts*.

speaker: narrator
text: Flip's phone buzzes. *Pickup reminder*.

speaker: gambler
text: Pickup? Who reads the *fine print*?

speaker: narrator
text: Eleven p.m. A rumble outside the *shop*.

speaker: narrator
text: Flip is back. A truck. And *four hundred people*.

speaker: gambler
text: Four hundred orders. Four hundred people. *Pay up*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit... can he *do* that?

speaker: bit
text: Every order needs the account holder's *ID*.

speaker: narrator
text: The first stranger steps up. Jay checks the *name*.

speaker: hero
text: Order one. Name on the account... *F. Lipp*.

speaker: bit
text: Order two. *F. Lipp*. Order three. *F. Lipp*.

speaker: narrator
text: All four hundred accounts. *Same name*.

speaker: friend
text: And only one F. Lipp is *standing here*.

speaker: narrator
text: The hired crowd shrugs and walks *home*.

speaker: gambler
text: Fine! One item. I take the *robot*.

speaker: narrator
text: Midnight. Three hundred ninety nine orders *cancelled*.

speaker: narrator
text: Flip walks out with one robot. For *one cent*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay sits alone among three hundred ninety nine *toys*.

speaker: hero
text: I saved the toys. But I lost *Theo's* robot.

speaker: bit
text: Grandma Penny would have hated the *Drop*, wouldn't she?

speaker: hero
text: No. She'd hate that *nobody* won.

speaker: hero
text: Bit. Tomorrow we run it again. *One change*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay writes it on a card in Grandma's *handwriting*.

speaker: narrator
text: Saturday, six a.m. The crowd is *back*.

speaker: hero
text: New rule. Every toy is the *only one*.

speaker: narrator
text: The prices start falling. And *this time*...

speaker: narrator
text: a man grabs a train set at *thirty dollars*.

speaker: soldier
text: I'm not risking it. My son *loves* trains.

speaker: bit
text: Falling clock rule. Whoever wants it most *buys first*.

speaker: narrator
text: Puzzles. Dolls. Kites. One by one, *everything* sells.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia guards her sweater. Twenty dollars. *Still not yet*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the door opens. It's *Theo*.

speaker: narrator
text: Behind him, Flip. With the robot. *A hundred twenty*.

speaker: gambler
text: Kid followed me for blocks. Market price. *Take it*.

speaker: hero
text: Flip. What did you pay for that? *One cent*.

speaker: hero
text: I'll buy it back. Forty dollars. *Original price*.

speaker: gambler
text: Forty times four thousand. Deal, *sucker*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay gives Theo the robot. Theo pays *eleven dollars*.

speaker: narrator
text: Closing time. Jay counts the *register*.

speaker: bit
text: Eight thousand nine hundred sixty. We're short *forty dollars*.

speaker: hero
text: Forty dollars. The price of *one robot*.

speaker: bit
text: Rent is due Monday. Nothing is left *to sell*.

speaker: narrator
text: Well... *almost* nothing.

speaker: narrator
text: On the last rack, the ugly sweater. *One cent*.

speaker: friend
text: One cent. I finally *won*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia takes it. And slaps down *forty dollars*.

speaker: hero
text: Mia, the price is *one cent*!

speaker: friend
text: Fair price. It makes *two* people happy.

speaker: narrator
text: Nine thousand dollars. The rent is *paid*.

speaker: narrator
text: Sunday, a photo arrives. Theo's sister. And a *robot*.

speaker: narrator
text: And Flip? His toys are gone. *Zero sales*.

speaker: gambler
text: Who pays triple when the Drop is *next door*?

speaker: narrator
text: Monday morning. One last item in the *sale bin*.

speaker: narrator
text: It's Bit. With a price tag on his *head*.

speaker: bit
text: One million dollars. Falling every minute. *Act fast*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit, get out. You're *not for sale*.

speaker: bit
text: Correct. I'm *priceless*.

speaker: narrator
text: Follow for a new What if every day.
